source.section: PDF page 10, Line 48b Example 1 (Anna: 30,000 Teachers' Retirement System + 38,000 XYZ pension, subtracts 68,000 on Line 48b, nothing on Line 45); PDF page 9, Line 45; PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = public pension (CT) 30,000.00 + private pension 38,000.00 = 68,000.00. Federal taxable income = 68,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 50,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 68,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 68,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 48b pension and annuity (Line 5b part): federal AGI 68,000.00 is under the 75,000.00 test, decimal 1; 68,000.00 x 1 = 68,000.00 -> 68,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 68,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 68,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 68,000.00 - 68,000.00 = 0.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 0.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 0.00 is not more than 30,000.00, exemption 15,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 0.00 - 15,000.00 = 0.00 (floored at 0). Line 4 Table B on 0.00 = 0.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 0.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 0.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.75 (Connecticut AGI 0.00, lowest band); Line 9 = 0.00 x 0.75 = 0.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: The booklet's Example 1: below the threshold the 100% Line 48b subtraction beats the 50% teachers' subtraction (they cannot be combined). The projection cannot tell a teachers' pension from another public pension and gives the same 68,000 on Line 48b, so it agrees with the booklet here.
